name: ecmascript-digit-class-matches
note: the '\d' token is the ECMAScript digit class, so 'id-\d' matches 'id-7' and routes to cloud. Under a non-ECMAScript grammar '\d' is a literal 'd' and this input has no 'id-d', so it would miss; the case therefore locks the ECMAScript dialect.

name: ecmascript-digit-class-not-literal-d
note: '\d' matches a digit, not a literal 'd': 'id-draft' has no digit after 'id-', so 'id-\d' misses and routing falls back to default. A grammar that read '\d' as literal 'd' would match here, so this case locks the ECMAScript reading from the other side.
